notes: Customer background: mid-size direct-to-consumer retailer, ~120 employees. Uses conversational search and an FAQ chat on storefront + post-purchase support.
Primary ask: hosted API that's cheap and easy to start; wants clear behavior under bursts and practical guidance to avoid 429-driven UX regressions.

Traffic profile: steady baseline ~8-12 req/s (low token avg), marketing blasts drive short bursts ~80-200 req/s for 45-90s; checkout flows can create short concurrency spikes (webhook fan-out + bot + live chat).

Observed during sandbox: scripted promo test produced 429s after sustained 90-120 req/s for ~60s. Devs saw no graceful retry pattern in place; frontend currently retries immediately causing amplification.
Key technical requirements called out in call:
- Per-api-key rate limits + per-route soft quotas (they want chat vs embeddings treated separately).
- Burst handling: allow short high-rate bursts (60-120s) without immediate 429; auto-burst credit or configurable burst window preferred.
- Clear 429 payloads and headers: need recommended Retry-After, remaining_quota headers to implement exponential backoff with jitter on frontend.
- Concurrency limit visibility: want realtime metrics (concurrency, queue length) surfaced in Console during POC.
- Fallbacks: prefer automatic model-fallback (to cheaper smaller model) rather than client-side blocking on 429s for non-critical interactions.
Security asks: SOC2 compliance, audit logs for requests, and optional request/response retention controls for 30/90/365 days. Legal currently OK with hosted cloud if SOC2 and audit logging present.
Cost sensitivity: SMB budget; wants guidance to tradeoff batching vs latency for embeddings so they can minimize cost during non-peak hours.
Quote from product lead: 'We can tolerate some throttling on background embeddings but chat must stay responsive — 200ms median target.'

Implementation notes from SE: propose two lanes — chat endpoints with higher concurrency, embeddings endpoints with queued batching + longer retry windows. Suggest dynamic route-level quotas and short-term burst allowance (token-bucket style) for promos.

Suggested POC plan: 1) define representative routes and traffic script; 2) run staged bursts up to 250 req/s; 3) validate 429 semantics, retry guidance, and auto-fallback rules; 4) review cost delta with quantization/batching suggestions.
Next AE action: share POC test harness template + recommended SDK retry snippet; sync calendar for kickoff (Maya to propose 2/08).
